description: Standard deduction of a taxpayer who can be claimed as a dependent: the greater of $4,000 or earned income plus $450, not more than the regular standard deduction.
disguised: Baseline allowance for a supported filer: a supported filer may subtract at least $4,000 (or labor receipts plus a small add-on), capped at the ordinary allowance.

description: Standard deduction of a taxpayer who can be claimed as a dependent: the greater of $8,000 or earned income plus $450, not more than the regular standard deduction.
disguised: Baseline allowance for a supported filer: a supported filer may subtract at least $8,000 (or labor receipts plus a small add-on), capped at the ordinary allowance.

description: Standard deduction of a taxpayer who can be claimed as a dependent: the greater of $12,000 or earned income plus $450, not more than the regular standard deduction.
disguised: Baseline allowance for a supported filer: a supported filer may subtract at least $12,000 (or labor receipts plus a small add-on), capped at the ordinary allowance.

description: Married filing separately: rate-bracket thresholds and the standard deduction are 1.5 times their former amounts (standard deduction $21,900).
disguised: Spouses who submit individual returns: every band edge in the graduated schedule and the flat allowance are scaled by 1.5 (allowance $21,900).

description: Married filing separately: rate-bracket thresholds and the standard deduction are 2 times their former amounts (standard deduction $29,200).
disguised: Spouses who submit individual returns: every band edge in the graduated schedule and the flat allowance are scaled by 2 (allowance $29,200).

description: Child tax credit: the phase-out threshold for married filing separately is $300,000.
disguised: Per-minor family offset: tapering for spouses on individual returns starts above $300,000 of modified income.

description: Child tax credit: the phase-out threshold for married filing separately is $400,000.
disguised: Per-minor family offset: tapering for spouses on individual returns starts above $400,000 of modified income.

description: Net investment income tax: the threshold for married filing separately is $200,000.
disguised: Surcharge on passive returns: for spouses on individual returns it applies above $200,000 of modified income.

description: Net investment income tax: the threshold for married filing separately is $250,000.
disguised: Surcharge on passive returns: for spouses on individual returns it applies above $250,000 of modified income.

description: Married filing separately: the standard deduction is $21,900 (1.5 times its former amount).
disguised: Spouses who submit individual returns may subtract a flat $21,900.

description: Married filing separately: the standard deduction is $29,200 (2 times its former amount).
disguised: Spouses who submit individual returns may subtract a flat $29,200.

description: Refundable child tax credit: phases in at 30% of earned income above $2,500 (was 15%).
disguised: Per-minor family offset, payable portion: accrues at 30% of labor receipts above a small floor.

description: Refundable child tax credit: phases in at 50% of earned income above $2,500 (was 15%).
disguised: Per-minor family offset, payable portion: accrues at 50% of labor receipts above a small floor.

description: Long-term capital gains: the 0% rate applies to single filers with taxable income up to $150,000.
disguised: Disposals of long-held property by unattached filers: no levy on the first $150,000 of taxable income.

description: Long-term capital gains: the 0% rate applies to single filers with taxable income up to $250,000.
disguised: Disposals of long-held property by unattached filers: no levy on the first $250,000 of taxable income.

description: Tax on a child's unearned income at the parent's rate applies to children under 10 (students too).
disguised: Supported-minor passive-receipts rule: applies to minors below 10 years, enrolled or not.

description: Tax on a child's unearned income at the parent's rate applies to children under 12 (students too).
disguised: Supported-minor passive-receipts rule: applies to minors below 12 years, enrolled or not.

description: Tax on a child's unearned income at the parent's rate applies only above 5 times the dependent standard-deduction floor.
disguised: Supported-minor passive-receipts rule: the first 5 baseline allowances of passive receipts are exempt.

description: Tax on a child's unearned income at the parent's rate applies only above 10 times the dependent standard-deduction floor.
disguised: Supported-minor passive-receipts rule: the first 10 baseline allowances of passive receipts are exempt.
